palette.notes: Frames: whole scenes tinted one hue (blood red, magenta-pink, ochre-orange, lilac) with deep teal/navy shadows. Drifter's red-pink cape and cyan sword are the constant accents; boss eyes glow violet-white.

lighting: Light is colour: a full-scene tint does the mood, glowing points (violet eyes, white orbs, cyan blade) do the highlights. Blackout frames with only white lightning are used as dramatic beats.
silhouette: Drifter is a tiny triangle of red cape with a dark head and a cyan line for the sword; it reads even at about 20 px tall against a screen-filling colossus. Bosses are huge, chunky, symmetric skulls.

motion.timing: Not measured. The boss reveal holds the Drifter still for many seconds while the giant's colours and debris change; action itself is quick dashes and slashes with particle bursts.
principles: contrast of fast action and slow ambience

texture: Big flat colour planes with stepped, blocky edges; the colossus breaks into scattered black pixel particles as it disintegrates. Ruins tiled with simple geometric glyphs; foliage as bold red/teal clusters.
camera: Static, centred framing for set pieces: the hero small on a staircase at bottom, the threat filling the top. Top-down view in play rooms; occasional tight close-up of the hunched, coughing Drifter.
sound: Moody synth score by Disasterpeace carries much of the story.

acting.enters: Appears as a tiny figure in total darkness, walks into place, then the lightning reveals the giant behind.
acting.acts: Stands still on the stairs, sword out, while the giant does the acting; in close-up he collapses and coughs. Talk is pictures, no words.
acting.exits: Dashes away, leaving the scene to dissolve or hold empty.
acting.depth: Pure scale contrast: tiny hero at the bottom, colossus filling the frame behind; a companion dog or figure appears small beside him.

techniques: one-hue scene tint (red, magenta, ochre) with teal shadows
blackout + lightning flash to reveal the big threat
tiny hero vs screen-filling giant for scale
glowing points as the only highlights
smear frame on the sword swing
feel: one-hue scene tint + teal shadows + tiny still hero vs huge glowing giant = epic mood with almost no animation
for_fred: Stage a reveal: black frame, Fred small at the bottom, a flash shows a huge shape behind him, Fred holds still while the scene tint changes. Let the big thing do the moving and Fred do the reaction; it needs very few frames.
